papers.title_in_file: Towards Arbitrary QUBO Optimization: Analysis of Classical and Quantum-Activated Feedforward Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a feedforward neural network optimizer for QUBO problems and tests whether a quantum-annealer activation function helps.

assertions.value: The authors report that their classical feedforward neural network optimizer reaches accuracy over 99% in less than 1.1 seconds on high-degree MaxCut and dense random QUBO problems, and that against Gurobi the achieved accuracy was comparable while the runtime was 2 to 3 orders of magnitude shorter on larger problems.
quotes: achieving accuracy over 99% in less than 1.1 seconds
While the achieved accuracy was comparable, FNN exhibited a significant runtime advantage over Gurobi for larger problems, outperforming it by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The winning model here is classical, not quantum.

assertions.value: The authors report that integrating a quantum annealer as a quantum activation function offered no benefit to the classical feedforward network, mainly because the quantum layer was deactivated.
quotes: such a combination offers no benefit to the classical FNN mainly due to the deactivation of the quantum layer
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study (simulation of the quantum layer).
assertions.reader_inference: A negative result for the quantum-activated hybrid in this setting.

assertions.value: The authors state that further research is needed to understand the interaction between quantum and classical components in hybrid networks.
quotes: further research is needed to better understand the interaction between quantum and classical components in hybrid networks
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its study.

papers.title_in_file: NAPA: Intermediate-level Variational Native-pulse Ansatz for Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2208.01215v5; its filename says PAN but its title is NAPA, the record's paper. Same paper, retitled across versions.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes NAPA, a native-pulse ansatz generator for variational quantum algorithms, tested on VQE tasks on simulators and IBM devices.

assertions.value: The authors report that on NISQ machines NAPA decreased latency by an average of 86% and reached 96.482% and 99.336% accuracy for VQE tasks on H2 and HeH+ respectively.
quotes: NAPA obtained improved the performance with decreased latency by an average of 86%
NAPA is able to achieve 96.482% and 99.336% accuracy for VQE tasks on H2 and HeH+ respectively
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that gradients are not available when the pulse ansatz is trained on NISQ machines, so a non-gradient optimizer is used.
quotes: gradients are not available as we train the pulse ansatz on NISQ machines. Therefore, we have to use a nongradient optimizer to train the parameters in the ansatz.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that how to explore the applications of NAPA on different types of variational quantum algorithms remains an open question.
quotes: How to explore the applications of NAPA on different types of VQAs remains an open question.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit.

papers.title_in_file: Implementing arbitrary quantum operations via quantum walks on a cycle graph
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a quantum neural network based on a discrete-time quantum walk on a cycle graph and proves it can realize any unitary operation.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the discrete-time quantum walk neural network on a cycle graph is universal for all unitary operations on the overall Hilbert space.
assertions.anchor: Theorem 1, Section III, p.4; proof in Appendix A
quotes: proved that the DTQW-QNN is universal for all unitary operations on the overall Hilbert space of the involved
it is universal as we show that any unitary operation
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (Section III), proof in Appendix A.

assertions.value: The authors state that their optimized scheme bounds the circuit depth, but that this is only a theoretical worst-case limit and that finding the appropriate number of nodes for a given task is an open question.
quotes: this is only a theoretical limit of the network size in the worst case for the purpose of analytical proof. The appropriate number of nodes for each task may vary, and it is an open question to find this number for a given task.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit.

assertions.value: The authors report good approximations of unitary operations on a Hilbert space up to 40 dimensions, and of arbitrary two-outcome POVMs, in numerical simulation.
quotes: We have shown good approximations of unitary operations on a Hilbert space up to 40 dimensions, as well as arbitrary two-outcome POVMs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Circuit Design using a Progressive Widening Enhanced Monte Carlo Tree Search
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a gradient-free Monte Carlo tree search with progressive widening for quantum architecture search in variational quantum algorithms.

assertions.value: The authors report that, compared with previous Monte Carlo tree search research, their technique reduces the number of quantum circuit evaluations by a factor of 10 up to 100 while achieving equal or better results, and the circuits have up to three times fewer CNOT gates.
quotes: Compared to previous MCTS research, our technique reduces the number of quantum circuit evaluations by a factor of 10 up to 100 while achieving equal or better results.
the resulting quantum circuits exhibit up to three times fewer CNOT gates
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that scaling their method to larger quantum circuits and other application domains may be a potential limitation, and that the experiments of the main results sections are noiseless simulations.
quotes: Although the scaling of PWMCTS to larger quantum circuits and different domains of application may be a potential limitation
Note that all the experiments, described in the previous section, are based on noiseless simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope and limits.

assertions.value: The authors report that under simulated noise on the hydrogen molecule ground-state energy problem, the method does not compete with the classical SCF and FCI benchmarks, though more search simulations significantly improve the results.
quotes: Figure 11a shows that PWMCTS does not manage to compete with the results of the classical SCF and FCI benchmarks. However, increasing the number of PWMCTS simulations significantly improves the results.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Algorithm Exploration using Application-Oriented Performance Benchmarks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: QED-C consortium paper extending its application-oriented quantum benchmark suite with HHL, hydrogen lattice VQE, error mitigation and a machine learning classifier.

assertions.value: The authors report, for the hydrogen lattice VQE benchmark, a decrease in accuracy with increased number of qubits but only a mild increase in the execution time.
quotes: We observe a decrease in accuracy with increased number of qubits, but only a mild increase in the execution time.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that applying the benchmark to a binary classification problem revealed an increase in training time for larger ansatz circuits and a significant classical overhead.
quotes: Applying this to a binary classification problem revealed the increase in training time required for larger anzatz circuits, and the significant classical overhead.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their machine learning benchmark is an early-stage version of a simple image classification problem.
assertions.anchor: Section VII Summary and Conclusions, p.21
quotes: Lastly, we presented an early-stage version of a machine learning algorithm, a simple image classification problem
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the scope of its machine learning benchmark.

papers.title_in_file: Impact of Amplitude and Phase Damping Noise on Quantum Reinforcement Learning: Challenges and Opportunities
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: Analytical and numerical study of how amplitude and phase damping noise affect a single-qubit quantum reinforcement learning algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors report, for specific examples of a quantum reinforcement learning algorithm, that the presence of noise does not necessarily hinder the performance and can in some cases have a beneficial effect.
quotes: we have shown that the presence of noise does not necessarily hinder the algorithm performance; in some cases, it can even have a beneficial effect.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical and numerical result from one study on a single qubit.

assertions.value: The authors report that phase damping noise influences both stationary-state fidelities symmetrically, while amplitude damping noise introduces an asymmetry favoring convergence to the ground state over the excited state.
quotes: While PDN influences both fidelities symmetrically, ADN introduces an asymmetry, favoring convergence to the ground state over the excited state.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical and numerical result from one study on a single qubit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work is restricted to a single qubit and that generalization to more qubits is left for future research.
quotes: In this work, for the sake of clarity and simplicity in the description, we have restricted ourselves to the case of a single qubit.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope.

papers.title_in_file: Approximate Quantum Random Access Memory Architectures
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a trainable parametric-circuit approximate QRAM and tests it on binary classification data loading and binary data storage.

assertions.value: The authors report that a QNN fed by their QRAM reaches 100% classification accuracy by the 6th epoch, against around the 10th and 15th epochs for the other two setups, with loss 0.53 against 0.89 for the fully connected network and 0.48 for the QNN with normal embedding.
quotes: We show that QRAM + QNN converges (with 100% classification accuracy) faster i.e., by 6th epoch, compared to the other two setups which converge at around 10th and 15th epochs.
The loss for QRAM + QNN (0.53) is less than FCNN setup (0.89) and comparable to QNN with normal embedding (0.48).
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on a small binary digits task.
assertions.reader_inference: The classification task is two digit classes, so the result may not carry to harder data.

assertions.value: The authors report that as address and data lines increase from 2 to 9, Hamming distance rises from 0 to 3.97 and the percentage of correct predictions falls from 100% to 0.58%.
quotes: We observe an increase in HD from 0 to 3.97 and decrease in percentage of correct predictions from 100% to 0.58% as we increase the number of address and data lines from 2 to 9.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QRAM circuit structure was kept fixed in all experiments and that the QRAM does not support storage of incremental data.
quotes: In all the experiments performed, the PQC structure of the QRAM is kept fixed, and also the QRAM does not support storage of incremental data.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope and limits.

papers.title_in_file: Improving Quantum Classifier Performance in NISQ Computers by Voting Strategy from Ensemble Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes EQV, an ensemble of variational quantum classifiers across IBM quantum computers combined by plurality voting, tested on MNIST digits.

assertions.value: The authors report that on real NISQ machines their ensemble reaches up to 16.0% and 6.1% higher accuracy than the state of the art on two-class and four-class classification.
assertions.anchor: Section V Conclusion and Discussion, p.5
quotes: On real NISQ machines, we are able to achieve up to 16.0% and 6.1% higher accuracy compared with state-of-the-art on two- and four-class classifications.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on IBM devices.

assertions.value: The authors state that the two-class experiment uses a training set of 300 MNIST-2 images and a test set of 30 MNIST-2 images, with digits one and nine.
quotes: The training set for two-class classification consists of 300 MNIST-2 images, and the test set consists of 30 MNIST-2 images. The two classes are made up of digits one and nine.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: A 30 image test set is small, so the reported accuracy gains carry wide uncertainty.

assertions.value: The authors point out that simple average aggregation in classical ensemble learning may not work well for NISQ computers because of the unbalanced confidence distribution in the variational quantum classifier.
quotes: We also point out that the simple average aggregation in classical ensemble learning may not work well for NISQ computers due to the unbalanced confidence distribution in VQC.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim, supported only by the paper's own figures.
